channel.title: World News
channel.description: Aggregated headlines linking to original publishers

item.title: Canary Islands struggle to cope after massive influx of migrants
item.description: Nearly 2,200 migrants have reached Spain’s Canary Islands by boat over the past two days, Spain’s maritime rescue service said on Sunday. The archipelago off northwest Africa is a major entry point for migrants, mainly from West Africa, attempting the dangerous Atlantic crossing in makeshift boats.

item.title: Ukraine strikes Crimea bridge as Zelensky says Starshield caps helping Russian attacks
item.description: Ukraine has struck the bridge linking Russia and ⁠Crimea across the Kerch strait, limiting the flow of traffic, the peninsula's Russian-backed governor Sergei Aksyonov ⁠said on Monday. It comes after Russia struck energy and railway infrastructure across Ukraine over the weekend, in attacks President Volodymyr Zelensky said were made possible ⁠partly due to restrictions on Ukraine's use of SpaceX's Starshield service.

item.title: 'Not a minute longer': Israel's Eisenkot calls for Netanyahu's ouster
item.description: Israeli prime ministerial hopeful Gadi Eisenkot on Sunday said caretaker premier Benjamin Netanyahu "cannot remain at the head of the government for a minute longer", following press reports that Netanyahu's office tried to frame members of an Arab-Israeli party ahead of last month's election.

item.title: Francophonie summit postpones new leader vote amid DR Congo-Rwanda dispute
item.description: The Organisation Internationale de la Francophonie (OIF) on Monday had been set to choose its new secretary general during talks in the Cambodian capital Phnom Penh. But delegates decided to postpone the election for a year after a walkout threat by the Democratic Republic of Congo amid an ongoing dispute between Kinshasa and Kigali.

item.title: WATCH: 'Cat Tour' brings together cat lovers in Massachusetts
item.description: ABC News' Danny New explains how feline lovers recently got their fix in Somerville, Massachusetts.

item.title: Man jailed for life for attempted murder of children that sparked Dublin riots
item.description: A man who attempted to murder three children as they waited outside their school in Dublin has been sentenced to life in prison.

item.title: Trump heads to Asia for 2nd high-stakes meeting with Chinese President Xi
item.description: Questions remain about the Nvidia CEO's relationship with alleged Chinese spy.

item.title: Verdict week in the Myanmar genocide case
item.description: PRESS REVIEW – Monday, November 16: The international press looks ahead to a verdict that could find the state of Myanmar guilty of genocide against the Rohingya minority. In other news, French journalists lift the lid on the many trials involving child prostitution. And finally, in Ireland, a cache of 12,000 once-banned books is back in the spotlight.

item.title: Trump heads to Asia to meet with Xi and Putin amid Nvidia fallout
item.description: The trip to China marks Trump's second time this year, and comes as the president and his party faced widespread backlash from voters in the recent midterm elections. (Image credit: Kevin Dietsch)

item.title: These birds fly 17,000 miles every year. Climate change could make it harder
item.description: Migratory birds cross the entire globe, carefully timing their journeys with the seasons. In a hotter climate, that timing is increasingly out of sync. (Image credit: Ryan Kellman)

item.title: As millions lose food aid nationwide, this SNAP office is doubling up as a food pantry
item.description: The cuts and changes to SNAP have been difficult for government workers who take pride in helping others. In San Diego, workers said they couldn't sit back while their neighbors went hungry. (Image credit: Kori Suzuki for NPR)

item.title: NPR's Student Podcast Challenge is back for 2027
item.description: The annual audio competition for grades four through 12 returns in January. Now in its ninth year, the contest has involved more than 90,000 students around the country.

item.title: Why sleep matters when it comes to weight gain and loss
item.description: Sleep can have a powerful impact on weight. Research shows it can affect appetite. There is also a two-way relationship between sleep quality and diet.

item.title: Breaking taboos: Egypt's sexual revolution takes to social media
item.description: In Egypt, a sexual revolution is quietly unfolding on social media. Accounts followed by tens of thousands of people, with posts attracting millions of views, are tackling a wide range of issues surrounding sexuality – from the widespread practice of female genital mutilation (which 93 per cent of women in rural areas have undergone) to sex education and sexual pleasure.

item.title: Iran live updates: Tanker attacked in Strait of Hormuz, UKMTO says
item.description: President Donald Trump announced "major combat operations" against Iran on Feb. 28.

item.title: At least 17 people killed in two separate shootings in South Africa
item.description: At least 17 people have been killed in two separate shootings in South Africa, police said on Monday.

item.title: Xi, Trump and Putin to discuss 'world peace' at Shenzhen summit, China says
item.description: The Chinese foreign ministry on Monday said that President Xi Jinping and his US and Russian counterparts Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin would discuss "safeguarding world peace and promoting strategic stability" when they hold their first trilateral summit in Shenzhen this week. The meeting is expected to happen on Thursday on the sidelines of a summit of Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) leaders.

item.title: Snow warning for large part of the UK
item.description: A yellow warning for snow and travel disruption has been issued across a large part of the UK by the Met Office.

item.title: Lula to govern Brazil for fourth term but faces challenges. Here’s what to know
item.description: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva has won a surprise reelection victory but faces significant challenges

item.title: Nations League: France defeat Turkey to advance to quarter-finals
item.description: France struggled at times but defeated Turkey (2-1) in the Nations League matchday. France finished first in group A1 and qualified for the quarter-finals.

item.title: Live: 600 Ukrainian drones target Moscow, Crimea bridge strike halts traffic
item.description: Russian air defences intercepted 600 Ukrainian drones flying towards the Moscow region overnight and into Monday morning, Moscow Mayor Sergey Sobyanin said. Ukraine also struck the bridge linking Russia and Crimea across the Kerch straight, the peninsula's Russia-backed governor said. Follow our liveblog for all the latest developments.

item.title: Australian MP who lost her legs in alleged attack speaks on leaving hospital
item.description: Helen Haines, the Australian politician who lost both legs after an alleged attack, has said she is "full of gratitude" upon leaving hospital.

item.title: Man charged after two killed in police chase collision
item.description: A man has been charged with causing death by dangerous driving after two people were killed when a car being chased by police collided with their vehicle.

item.title: Five EU nations set to announce migrant deportation centre deal with Rwanda
item.description: Five EU countries on Monday are set to announce a deal to establish a migrant deportation centre in Rwanda – the first such facility outside the bloc. The move comes after the EU toughened its migration rules in late 2025.

item.title: William and Kate land in Mumbai for Earthshot Prize trip
item.description: The Prince and Princess of Wales have arrived ‌in Mumbai for the Earthshot Prize awards, ‌marking the couple's first official trip overseas in nearly four years.

item.title: Eisenkot says Netanyahu ‘cannot remain’ after alleged election interference by aide
item.description: Israeli prime ministerial hopeful Gadi Eisenkot said on Sunday caretaker premier Benjamin Netanyahu must leave office immediately following reports of alleged electoral interference by a Netanyahu aide. The former army chief called Netanyahu and his entourage an immediate threat to democracy, hours after representatives discussed forming a national unity government.

item.title: British women convicted of illegal abortions under Victorian-era law to receive automatic pardons
item.description: Women who were convicted or cautioned for illegal abortions will be automatically pardoned under a law change.

item.title: Hundreds of thousands of Czechs protest in Prague over public media funding plan
item.description: Hundreds of thousands of Czechs rallied in Prague on Sunday against government plans to replace public media fees with direct state funding, which critics say threatens broadcasters’ independence. Organisers said turnout exceeded a March protest of more than 200,000, potentially making it the largest demonstration since the 1989 Velvet Revolution.

item.title: WATCH: Passenger jet collides with UPS plane on taxiway at Miami International Airport
item.description: A UPS cargo plane and a Copa Airlines passenger jet collided on a taxiway at Miami International Airport on Saturday night, according to airport officials and the FAA.

item.title: Flight disruptions expected to last into Monday
item.description: Congress recently gave the Department of Transportation $12.5 billion to upgrade the aging air traffic control system. President Trump wants more. (Image credit: Tom Brenner)

item.title: Government accused of 'complacency' over 'catastrophic' security risks to UK
item.description: Andy Burnham's government appears "complacent" about the potential for "catastrophic risks" to the UK - and the country is underprepared, an influential committee of peers has warned.

item.title: Sky News announces new hosts of Sunday Morning With…
item.description: Sky News has announced its hosting line-up for the next four episodes of its flagship Sunday morning current affairs programme.

item.title: Elon Musk, Uber co-founder join calls to reinstate Jensen Huang as Nvidia chief
item.description: Elon Musk and an Uber co-founder were among more than 158,000 signatories by Sunday demanding Jensen Huang’s reinstatement as Nvidia chief pending an independent investigation. Huang resigned Thursday after revelations of two extramarital affairs, one with a subordinate and another with a woman accused of spying for China, ending his 33-year tenure.

item.title: Mexican drug trade 'boss of bosses' Miguel Angel Felix Gallardo dies at 80
item.description: Miguel Angel Felix Gallardo, a founder of Mexico’s Guadalajara drug cartel known as the “boss of bosses”, died in hospital on Sunday aged 80 after suffering multiple organ failure, Jalisco state’s security ministry said. Imprisoned since 1989, he had been transferred from prison to the hospital two days before his death.

item.title: Far from home. Voyager 1 is now farther than anything man has sent into space
item.description: NASA's Voyager 1, which is the furthest man-made object from Earth, is set to reach a new milestone this week. On Wednesday, the probe will be roughly 16 billion miles from Earth. (Image credit: AP)

item.title: Kroupi on target as France beat Turkey to reach Nations League quarters
item.description: Eli Junior Kroupi scored his maiden goal for France as Les Bleus beat Turkey 2-1 in Bordeaux on Sunday to top their group with 13 points and qualify for the quarter-finals of the Nations League. World Cup winners Spain, who lost at home against England, are among their potential opponents in the last eight.

item.title: Who makes Sydney Sweeney's American Eagle jeans — and under what conditions?
item.description: Sydney Sweeney has great jeans, American Eagle Outfitters tells us. But who made them? And what are working conditions like in the garment factories of Pakistan and Bangladesh? (Image credit: Michael Nagle/Bloomberg)

item.title: PM to say 'Brexit hasn't worked' and set out conditions for future EU deal in major speech
item.description: The prime minister will call for a reset of Britain's relationship with Europe ahead of Friday's UK-EU summit - and assert that "the Brexit we were given has not worked".

item.title: Nearly 2,200 migrants reach Spain's Canary Islands in two days
item.description: Nearly 2,200 migrants have reached the Canary Islands over the past two days, Spain’s coastguard said Sunday, continuing a recent surge of arrivals from West African countries to the Spanish archipelago, where the authorities declared a migration emergency earlier this week.

item.title: Yemen's Houthis advance on Aden as government forces retreat to defend their capital
item.description: Houthi forces in Yemen have advanced to within 60 kilometres of Aden, the seat of the country's internationally recognised government, military and government sources said Sunday. The embattled government earlier announced it was pulling back its last forces from the Bab el-Mandeb Strait to defend its temporary capital on the southern coast of Yemen.

item.title: Prague's fight for public TV: Why a high-profile presenter is prepared to walk away
item.description: Daniel Stach, one of the Czech Republic’s best-known television presenters and science journalists, tells Gavin Lee on France 24 why he is prepared to walk away from his career rather than work under changes he believes threaten the independence of public broadcasting.

item.title: Van Hollen says Schumer's team trying to 'instill fear' to retain Senate leadership
item.description: Maryland Sen. Chris Van Hollen touted his chances of becoming Senate majority leader when Democrats take control of the Senate in January.

item.title: New Orleans port sues owners of tanker involved in Mississippi crash
item.description: Officials are seeking at least $1 million in damages from the owners of the tanker that hit a cruise ship last week. The incident was dubbed "the miracle on the Mississippi" after no one was killed. (Image credit: Gerald Herbert)

item.title: Company caught up in Nvidia controversy launches internal investigation
item.description: A cloud computing company facing scrutiny over claims involving tech giant Nvidia has launched an internal investigation conducted by external lawyers.

item.title: Estonia to close Russian border crossings after 'sabotage' attempt at drone factory
item.description: Estonia will close all its border crossing points with Russia from December 1, its ​foreign minister ‌said on Sunday, following a suspected ⁠sabotage attack on an Estonian defence company that Tallinn blamed on ‌Moscow. The Kremlin denied the accusations, calling them "entirely baseless".

item.title: How did over 2,000 migrants reach the Canaries in just 48 hours?
item.description: Spain says nearly 2,200 migrants have arrived by boat to the Canary Islands this weekend. The strip of the Atlantic Ocean between West Africa and the Canary Islands is one of the world's deadliest migration routes – and the journey is usually made with ill-equipped dinghies and overcrowded boats. Details by FRANCE 24 correspondent in Madrid, Sarah Morris.

item.title: WATCH: World Sanfilippo Awareness Day
item.description: This global campaign brings public awareness and attention to Sanfilippo Syndrome, a rare, terminal genetic disorder that causes dementia in children for which there is currently no cure.

item.title: Israel kills senior member of Hamas's military wing in Gaza strike
item.description: The Israeli military said on Sunday its forces had killed a senior member of Hamas's military wing in Gaza. The militant group confirmed the death of Samir Abu Younis, the commander of its Rafah brigade, adding that he played a prominent role in planning the October 7, 2023 attacks.

item.title: ATC routers' ability to broadcast data turned off, being investigated: Duffy
item.description: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy joined "This Week" following a rare nationwide ground stop that brought air travel to a halt Friday.

item.title: 'Record number of women elected' to US Congress & governorships in midterm elections
item.description: Following the 2026 US midterm elections, Gavin Lee welcomes Politico Senior National Politics Reporter Lauren Fedor to discuss the growing number of Democratic women elected to Congress and governorships, particularly mothers of young children.

item.title: Iran claims drone attack on US military base in Bahrain
item.description: Bahrain issued two alerts of potential threats on Sunday, its first such warnings since September as blasts rocked the capital, Manama. It comes after Iran targeted an airbase in the US-allied island state, ending a long lull in strikes during the Middle East War and comes as negotiations to end the conflict remain at a stalemate, with the US maintaining its naval blockade and Iran its stranglehold over the strait of Hormuz. Story by Rachael Griffiths.

item.title: Trump to meet with Putin and Xi in China, US officials say
item.description: Trump will participate in the first-ever trilateral meeting between the leaders of the U.S., China, and Russia on the sidelines of the APEC Summit in China next week.

item.title: WATCH: Skylar's big surprise by the New England Patriots
item.description: Sixteen-year-old Skylar, a pediatric cancer patient, got an extra surprise from New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye while spending a day baking with Ann Michael Maye.

item.title: Hamas says senior commander killed in Israeli airstrike
item.description: A senior Hamas commander who helped plan and oversee the 7 October 2023 attack had been killed in an Israeli airstrike, according to the Palestinian militant group.

item.title: WATCH: Elementary school named after beloved custodian
item.description: Marilyn Hampton was a beloved custodian for the Aubrey Independent School District outside Dallas, Texas. She was surprised with a school named in her honor, Marilyn Hampton Elementary School.

item.title: Microsoft confirms all services are restored after global outage
item.description: Microsoft has said that all services have been fully restored after a global outage which affected the NHS, police, schools and other services across the UK.

item.title: US asked if Ukraine would give up parts of Donbas for NATO membership, Zelenskyy says
item.description: The US has asked for the first time whether Ukraine would withdraw from parts of the Donbas region if Kyiv were admitted to NATO, Volodymyr Zelenskyy said.

item.title: Trump, Xi and Putin to hold unprecedented meeting, White House says
item.description: The leaders of the US, China and Russia will hold an unprecedented meeting on the sidelines of a major economic summit, the White House has said.

item.title: Goalkeeper given 12-game ban for fatal collision with Tenerife striker
item.description: Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono has been suspended for 12 games after an on-field collision that resulted in the death of Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel.

item.title: LIVE: ABC News Live
item.description: 24/7 coverage of breaking news and live events

item.title: Lauren Boebert will lose her seat in Congress to Democrat Laubacher, AP projects
item.description: Colorado Republican Rep. Lauren Boebert will lose her House seat to Democratic challenger Eileen Laubacher, The Associated Press projected Friday.

item.title: Sarah Huckabee Sanders receives 2028 presidential encouragement
item.description: Supporters and donors have been encouraging GOP Arkansas Gov. Sarah Huckabee Sanders to run for president in the 2028 cycle, sources told ABC News.

item.title: Congressional Republicans push Howard Lutnick, Jensen Huang to testify about Nvidia
item.description: Senate Banking Committee Chairman Tim Scott, a Republican, sent letters to both Huang and Lutnick to publicly testify in front of the committee

item.title: Schumer and Van Hollen face off for Senate majority leader. What do Democrats think?
item.description: Within moments of Chris Van Hollen announcing his intent to challenge Chuck Schumer in a race to lead next year’s Senate Democratic majority, endorsements began flying.

item.title: WATCH: 41-year-old firefighter’s life saved by heart transplant
item.description: Nico Ratto, a dad of two from New Jersey, spent 45 days hospitalized before receiving a lifesaving heart transplant.

item.title: WATCH: Heartwarming update on Punch the Monkey
item.description: The baby macaque at Japan’s Ichikawa City Zoo became a viral sensation after turning to an IKEA toy for comfort. Nine months later, Punch has joined the troop and taken an interest in a baby macaque.

item.title: WATCH: Empire State Building climbers appear in court
item.description: The daredevil couple who were arrested after climbing to the top of the Empire State Building were in court on Thursday to face criminal charges and possible deportation.

item.title: Republicans dazed by midterm election defeats grapple with what went wrong
item.description: Republicans are grappling with unexpected losses after the midterm elections

item.title: WATCH: School's ultimate class trip heads to Antarctica
item.description: ABC News' Danny New reports on a group of middle schoolers in Maryland who are about to get the snow day of their lives in the form of a class trip to Antarctica.

item.title: WATCH: Tanker truck driver narrowly avoids train crash in Fort Worth
item.description: A tanker truck driver managed to escape from his vehicle just seconds before a train slammed into his truck.

item.title: Republicans push for Jensen Huang's testimony following Nvidia CEO's resignation
item.description: "I don't think he's got anything to hide now. Let it fly," Rep. Burchett said.

item.title: WATCH: United Airlines banning AI bots from booking flights
item.description: The airline says customers who give their personal and credit card information to AI businesses run the risk of having their sensitive data exposed.

item.title: WATCH: Mom becomes first woman to run 100 miles in Antarctica
item.description: ABC News' Danny New talks to a Canadian ultramarathoner becoming the first woman ever to run 100 continuous miles in Antarctica.
